plan_a_advantages: More focused on speed development with dedicated threshold tempo sessions.
Shorter tempo sessions minimize fatigue and risk of overtraining.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated hill session, which is beneficial for trail running strength and technique.
Longer runs in Plan B could be suitable for a runner with a higher weekly mileage base.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It strategically incorporates two threshold tempo sessions, which are crucial for building the sustainable speed needed for trail racing. Plan B, while including some hill work, relies heavily on longer, moderate-intensity runs, which are less effective for directly improving speed and power. Plan A’s structured approach to building threshold strength, combined with consistent easy runs, provides a more targeted and efficient pathway to faster trail running performance. Furthermore, the shorter duration of the tempo sessions in Plan A reduces the risk of overtraining compared to the longer tempo run in Plan B.
